author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page below the first as the first page
summary: A page value below the first page currently renders the error page. The owner listing must read any such value as the first page and show the normal listing.
acceptance_criteria: given a page of zero, when the owner listing is requested, then the first page of matching owners is listed and no error page is shown
given a page below zero, when the owner listing is requested, then the first page of matching owners is listed and no error page is shown
given no page stated at all, when the owner listing is requested, then the first page of matching owners is listed
given a page below the first one and a search matching no owner, when the owner listing is requested, then no error page is shown
non_goals: page values that are not whole numbers, such as text or fractions — undecided, recorded as an open question
the veterinarian directory's paging — outside this decision, recorded as an open question
any change to how a page beyond the last page behaves
notes: Intake recorded no decisions beyond the request (handoff.jsonl line 1); every scope statement here traces to that quoted request. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. PRD records the current error-page behavior as Owner records edge case 5 (known defect) and the new rule as edge case 4. No prd-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory already covers this slice unchanged. The owner listing's paging is an existing contract of OwnerController (system-design.md Contracts row, 'search with paging'), and the fix is boundary normalization of one request parameter inside the existing private pagination helper. No new type, package, or pattern. The behavior sits exactly where system-design.md Overview records business rules living today (controllers plus framework validation), so it neither widens nor narrows the open 'no service layer' question. security-principles.md Trust Boundaries places range checking of external input at the boundary, which is where the normalization belongs: the request parameter is normalized once on entry, and the code past it keeps trusting its contract. Basis for the coverage claim: read of OwnerController.java (processFindForm at :95, findPaginatedForOwnersLastName at :133) and of templates/owners/ownersList.html; the IDE oracle is not connected in this run, so this is the weaker grep-and-read basis rather than a symbol resolution.
integration_points: the currentPage model attribute set by addPaginationModel is consumed by the ownersList pager (numbered links, first/previous/next/last enablement)
findByLastNameStartingWith is called with the PageRequest built from the normalized page; the repository contract is unchanged

patterns.description: existing findPaginatedForOwnersLastName helper converting a one-based page into a zero-based PageRequest; the normalization belongs here or immediately before it, ahead of the repository call

risks.risk: the normalized page is used for the query but the raw value still reaches the model, so the pager renders a link to page 0 and enables the 'previous' control
risks.mitigation: pass the normalized page to addPaginationModel as well, so currentPage and the query agree; assert the rendered currentPage in the test, not only the listing view name

risks.risk: normalizing after the repository call would leave the fourth acceptance criterion failing, because PageRequest.of rejects a negative index before the empty-result branch is ever reached
risks.mitigation: normalize before the PageRequest is constructed; the 'page below the first plus a search matching no owner' criterion then falls out of the existing empty-result branch

notes: Autofix audit: the handoff log holds no design-doc-autofix records, so the audit is a no-op. Durable-memory write: docs/system-design.md Contracts row for OwnerController now carries REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 and states the guarantee; this is the only docs edit the verdict warrants and no ADR is due (no trade-off, no hard-to-reverse choice). system-design.md Known Defects does not list this behavior, so nothing there is retired. Scope guards: the vet listing declares its own page size and paging independently (Constants section) and is untouched; a page value that is not a whole number stays undecided in the PRD's open questions, so the slice must not add parsing or a custom binder that would silently decide it; behavior for a page beyond the last page is unchanged.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Not run, not clean: no NVD match was performed in this review. The OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, so `./gradlew dependencyCheckAnalyze` does not exist here, and this reviewer has no network access. Framework versions (Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Jackson) are therefore not verified against the NVD by this pass. Because the diff changes no dependency, that gap is pre-existing rather than introduced — closing it is a CI or human task, not a blocker for this change.

Pre-existing, out of scope for this change, recorded so it is not lost: the page parameter still has no upper bound. `/owners?page=2147483647` clamps to itself and reaches PageRequest.of(2147483646, 5), which becomes a very large OFFSET at the database. That unbounded-input path predates this change and the diff neither introduces nor widens it (security-principles.md: pre-existing absences are never findings), but a symmetric upper clamp against totalPages would be the natural companion to the lower clamp if the paging contract is revisited.
approved_aspects: Boundary normalization sits at the request boundary: the request-derived page is clamped once in processFindForm before it reaches either findPaginatedForOwnersLastName or addPaginationModel, so no unclamped value survives past the boundary (security-principles.md 'Validate at the boundary').

No injection surface introduced: the page value stays an int and reaches only PageRequest.of; the last-name search continues through the derived repository query findByLastNameStartingWith with no string-concatenated query text.
No new output escaping concern: the only new model attribute path is currentPage, an int, rendered under Thymeleaf's default escaping, which the change does not disable.

Removes an availability/error-disclosure path rather than adding one: page values below the first previously reached PageRequest.of with a negative index, throwing IllegalArgumentException into the error page that renders the underlying exception message. The clamp closes that reflected-exception path for this input class.

No secrets, credentials, or configuration values added anywhere in the diff (docs/prd.md, docs/system-design.md, OwnerController.java, OwnerControllerTests.java); no hardcoded URL, token, key, or password introduced.
No file I/O, no path composition from request input, no shell or process execution, no deserialization, no reflection, and no new regex in the change.

No new controller, endpoint, or request-bound type: the change edits an existing handler, so the mass-assignment and exposed-surface rows of security-principles.md are untouched, and no management-endpoint exposure widens.
No thread-safety regression: requestedPage is a method-local int in a singleton controller that gains no mutable state; the added FIRST_PAGE is a static final int constant.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle and settings.gradle are outside the change set, so no dependency is added, removed, or version-shifted by this diff. Test-only additions (JUnit ParameterizedTest, ValueSource) resolve from the already-declared spring-boot-starter-test.
